sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento delle tensioni geopolitiche in Medio Oriente e dell'impatto sulla produzione di petrolio. Il VIX è sceso a 17.08, ma rimane sopra la soglia di 15, indicando una certa incertezza. L'S&P 500 è sceso dello 0.38%, mentre il DXY è debole (-0.14%). Il prezzo del petrolio è salito (+0.69%) e il TLT è sceso (-0.50%).
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the impact on oil production. The VIX decreased to 17.08, but remains above the 15 threshold, indicating some uncertainty. The S&P 500 fell by 0.38%, while the DXY is weak (-0.14%). Oil prices rose (+0.69%) and TLT fell (-0.50%).

market_impact_summary.it: I mercati azionari sono deboli, con l'S&P 500 in calo dello 0.38%. Il settore energetico è sostenuto dal prezzo del petrolio in aumento (+0.69%). I tassi di interesse sono saliti, con il US 10Y Yield che raggiunge il 4.39% (+0.83%). Il dollaro è debole, con il DXY in calo dello 0.14%.
market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets are weak, with the S&P 500 down 0.38%. The energy sector is supported by rising oil prices (+0.69%). Interest rates have risen, with the US 10Y Yield reaching 4.39% (+0.83%). The dollar is weak, with the DXY down 0.14%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dello 0.2%, Shanghai pressoché invariato. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo dello 0.4%, il VIX è sceso a 17.08, in calo dell'1.8%. Il dollaro si è indebolito, con il DXY in calo dello 0.1%. L'oro è salito a 4733 dollari l'oncia, in rialzo dello 0.7%. Il petrolio Brent è in rialzo dello 0.7% a 100.75 dollari. I rendimenti dei titoli di stato USA sono saliti, con il decennale al 4.39%, in aumento dello 0.8%.

La banca centrale norvegese ha alzato i tassi d'interesse a causa dell'impatto del conflitto in Iran. La crisi dell'Iran sta avendo un impatto sui mercati asiatici, con una riduzione delle forniture di petrolio. L'integrazione finanziaria nell'area euro è migliorata nonostante la persistente frammentazione.

Oggi saranno resi noti i dati sui Non-Farm Payrolls e il tasso di disoccupazione negli Stati Uniti. Il mercato attende con ansia questi dati per capire l'andamento dell'economia americana.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin scende del 2,63% a settantanove mila e trecentotrentacinque dollari. I flussi degli ETF continuano positivi con un afflusso di quarantasei milioni di dollari. Il movimento odierno potrebbe essere influenzato da prese di profitto dopo recenti guadagni. 
  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum scende del 3,00% a duemiladuecentosessantanove dollari, Solana perde l'1,48% a ottantasette virgola ottantotto dollari e BNB cede l'1,95% a seicentotrentacinque virgola sessantotto dollari. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 38, in zona Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed down 0.2%, Shanghai essentially flat. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed down 0.4%, the VIX fell to 17.08, down 1.8%. The dollar weakened, with the DXY down 0.1%. Gold rose to $4,703 per ounce, up 0.7%. Brent crude oil is up 0.7% at $100.75 US Treasury yields rose, with the 10-year at 4.39%, up 0.8%. The Norwegian central bank raised interest rates due to the impact of the conflict in Iran. The Iran crisis is impacting Asian markets, with a reduction in oil supplies. Financial integration in the euro area has improved despite persistent fragmentation. Today, the Non-Farm Payrolls and unemployment rate data will be released in the United States. The market is eagerly awaiting these data to understand the trend of the American economy. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin falls 2.63% to $79,335 ETF flows continue positive with an inflow of $46 million. Today's movement could be influenced by profit-taking after recent gains. Among altcoins, Ethereum falls 3% to $2,269, Solana loses 1.48% to $87.88 and BNB drops 1.95% to $635.68 The Fear & Greed Index is at 38, in Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors. We are waiting for economic data releases. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The Iran War’s Strategic Fallout
articles.snippet: By leaving US allies and rivals alike scrambling to respond to an unpredictable and unreliable superpower, the war in the Middle East is driving an historic geopolitical realignment that will shift the global balance of power over the next decade. The scale of the changes will rival those following the end of the Cold War.

articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown discuss their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing stockpiles, subsidies, and trade restrictions,…

articles.title: Eurobonds: Despite objections, they are more needed than ever
articles.snippet: We argued last year that it was time to create a deep, large, and liquid market for Eurobonds (Blanchard and Ubide 2025). Since then, there has been growing support for the initiative, not just from think tanks and academics (Hildebrand, Rey, and Schularick 2025) but notably from the European Central Bank (ECB) (Lane 2026), the Bundesbank (Nagel, Politico, February 2026), and some EU governments (Cuerpo, in the Financial Times, February 2026, and at PIIE event). In this update, we discuss why the urgency to issue Eurobonds in large quantities has grown, clarify our proposal, and address the…

articles.title: The Pentagon Needs a Playbook for Munitions Surge Production
articles.snippet: The Tomahawk Land Attack Missiles the U.S. military fired during Operation Epic Fury take months to put on contract and years to produce.Whether driven by U.S. military operations or support to partners, the challenge of quickly replenishing U.S. munitions is not new. Exquisite munitions often take an exquisite amount of time to manufacture and deliver. Defense officials, in turn, frequently want to compress that time as much as possible, seeking to restock fast and mitigate future risks.The Russo-Ukrainian War has illuminated the challenge of accomplishing this feat. It also offers lessons for how the U.S can accelerate munitions production timelines The post The Pentagon Needs a Playbook for Munitions Surge Production appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Why These 5 Drone Stocks Could Outperform This Summer
articles.snippet: For decades, Western militaries have been sleepwalking into a strategic crisis. A crisis that the war in Ukraine revealed, and the escalating conflict in the Middle East is now making existential. Modern warfare is no longer dominated by tanks, jets, and billion-dollar weapons systems. Instead, it is defined by drones. Ukraine learned this lesson the hard way in 2024, when it had to produce an estimated 1.2 million drones to counter Russian advances on the battlefield. These weren’t fringe systems or experimental tools. They became the backbone…

articles.title: Chinese Firm Takes U.S. Banks to Court Over Pre-Sanction Payment Freeze
articles.snippet: Chinese fuel trader HY Energy is suing U.S. banking giants JP Morgan and Citigroup for blocked payments to a Chinese oil firm a year before the latter was sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury for dealing with Iranian oil, Bloomberg reports. HY Energy, a regional fuel trader in eastern China, alleges in two separate lawsuits filed in Shanghai and Beijing that JP Morgan and Citi failed to process and complete transfers for a total of $40 million to China Oil and Petroleum Company Limited (COPC) back in 2023. This was months before COPC was designated…
